designedAgainst.note: Design only. No runtime module imports this file; nothing here is available to a learner.

canDo: talk about their own everyday life in the present: what they do, where they live, how their day goes and roughly when
say who the people around them are and what those people are, simply
find their way in a place: ask where something is and understand a short answer
handle a small purchase end to end: choose, ask the price, understand the number, pay
say what they can and cannot do, and ask the same of someone else
arrange to meet somebody at a day, a time and a place
keep a conversation alive when they meet unknown language, by asking what a word means or how to say something
cannotYet: talk about the past in any form
talk about the future beyond a present-tense arrangement with a time word
give or follow directions of more than one step
explain a reason with a subordinate clause
describe people or places in more than one attribute
spell aloud, handle dates or months, or give personal contact details
sustain a conversation that changes topic more than once
definition.interactionCeiling: one situation, one topic, 10–12 meaningful turns, with repair available and support fading as evidence allows

canDos.why: After a name and an origin, what somebody does is the next thing every first conversation reaches. It is also the first statement about the learner's own life that is not a preference.
A learner who can only answer is still being interviewed. Asking is what makes the exchange mutual, and it is the level's first do-question.
The single largest everyday topic, and the one that turns a handful of verbs into a description of a life. Deliberately a few actions, not a timetable.
A routine without time is a list. This is the level's time anchor — part of the day, and the hour — and it is what later lets an arrangement exist at all.

The first repair that learns rather than pauses. Pre-A1 can stop a conversation it does not follow; this lets the learner take a word out of it and keep going, which is what makes more input survivable.
canDos.intentReuse: repair_request with a new repairKind subtype

canDos.why: Pre-A1 can introduce the learner. This turns a pair into a group, and it is the honest functional core of 'family' without a vocabulary list: this is X, X is Y.
The highest-value question a beginner can own in a real place. It converts every unknown building into something they can resolve without English fluency.

Asking without being able to answer leaves the learner on one side of the exchange. Two or three relations are enough — here, there, next to, near — and they are what makes a short answer comprehensible when they hear it.

Extends asking-where into moving, which is where beginners actually get stuck. Kept as a should-have because it opens a context of its own and the core autonomy is already covered by the two required location skills.
Ten is not enough for a price or a clock. The extension exists for those two uses and is introduced inside them, never as a counting lesson.
canDos.intentReuse: use_quantity with a level-aware taught range

canDos.why: Pre-A1 can ask for a thing politely but not find out what it costs, which makes every purchase a leap of faith.
The integrated transaction: choose, quantify, ask the price, understand the answer, close. It reuses the café shape Pre-A1 already owns and adds the money the café never mentioned.
Ability is how a beginner explains themselves in one sentence — what they can join, what they need help with. It is also the level's cheapest new grammar: one modal, no conjugation.
canDos.architecturalNote: The evaluator must tell ability-can from request-can; Pre-A1 already produces 'Can you repeat, please?'

canDos.why: Turns ability into an exchange and reuses the do-question shape in a second frame. Should rather than required: the level already has two required question forms.
The other half of learning from a conversation: not only what a word means but how to produce one they lack. Cheap — one frame — and it multiplies every other capability.
canDos.intentReuse: repair_request with a new repairKind subtype

canDos.why: The last required capability of the level, and the one that proves the rest: a day, a time, a place and a polite close, held together in one exchange. Nothing new is needed to say it — which is the point.

deferredToA2.why: A second tense doubles every pattern the level owns. It is the first A2 capability precisely because it is the obvious next unlock.
A present tense with a time word already arranges things. `going to` adds a form without adding a function A1 needs.
`because` turns one clause into two. Choice and preference work without it at this level.
Asking where something is and understanding a short answer is the autonomy; left/right/straight sequences are a comprehension load of their own.
One attribute is enough for A1 (`She's a student`). Adjective order, plurals and `there is/are` belong together, later.
Heard throughout A1, produced in A2. The morphology costs more than the capability it adds while `is` covers most needs.
Days of the week serve arrangements. Dates need ordinals and a second number system.
The alphabet is a system, not a phrase, and it pays off mainly with contact details this product does not collect.
A new context with its own vocabulary, when the transactional muscle A1 builds is already exercised by a shop and a counter.
Choosing works with `this one` at A1. Comparison is a structure with no A1 function.
Two adverbs make a routine truthful. Four make a grammar exercise.
Deliberate product decision: the curriculum never trains a learner to type real personal data.

optionalOrNotTaken.why: Cheap to say and rarely needed to act. Available as receptive input inside personal exchanges; not a required production.
Trimmed from the required set in review: `He's a student` already carries the function, and adjectives invite a catalogue.
A vocabulary set looking for a capability. If choosing ever needs it, `this one` is doing the work.
Mostly interface language, which the product already localises.

patterns.form: It's + here / there / next to / near + X
How much is it / are they?
Let's meet at + time / See you + day

proposed.whyNotExisting: An hour is neither a place nor an object; a slot that accepts it must reject 'Madrid' and 'water'.
`on Monday` and `at seven` are different slots with different prepositions; collapsing them would let the engine build 'on seven'.
`person` holds a name; a relation takes a possessive and cannot be substituted for one ('This is my Alex').
Only needed if the should-have transport episode is built; drop the type with the episode.

explicitlyNotNeeded.why: A workplace is a `place`; naming professions is a vocabulary list the level refuses.
A price is a number with a neutral unit; the evaluator compares the number.

intentStrategy.rule: One intent per communicative function. Variants travel as a subtype on the step payload, the way Pre-A1 already carries repairKind, quantityForm and thingId — not as a new intent.

newSubtypesOnExistingIntents.change: level-aware taught range so 11–100 counts as target evidence in A1 while Pre-A1 keeps 1–10

intentStrategy.explosionGuard: If an arc's design needs more than three new intents, the arc is teaching phrases rather than a capability.

evaluationStrategy.rule: The canonical frame is always judged locally. Escalation is for a reply that is inconclusive, exactly as Pre-A1 routes it. No capability is designed to depend on the provider being reachable.

arcs.communicativeProblem: A first conversation runs out after a name and an origin: the learner cannot say what fills their days, and cannot ask.
arcs.whyNow: It is the smallest step from Pre-A1's personal exchange, and it introduces the statement frame every later arc reuses.

miniStory.why: The arc's value is a two-way exchange, which roleplay carries better than a hosted story.

arcs.autonomyTarget: inherits Pre-A1 support; the model answer is available while the frame is new and withheld on the arc's last recall
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided statements and one unaided question per required can-do
arcs.risk: The statement frame invites a profession list. The budget is spent on the frame and on two or three neutral workplaces, not on jobs.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can say what they do but not when or how often, so they cannot describe a day or understand somebody else's.
arcs.whyNow: It extends the statement frame just learned, and it needs the level's time anchor, which everything later depends on.

miniStory.why: A day is a sequence; a hosted story lets the learner meet several actions in order and still answer in their own words.

arcs.autonomyTarget: support fades where the frame is reused; new time language keeps a hint
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided routine statements including a time, and one unaided meaning question
arcs.risk: Three new pattern groups in one arc is the level's densest moment. The verb budget is five actions and the frequency set is two adverbs.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can introduce themselves but not anybody else, so a conversation with two other people is closed to them.
arcs.whyNow: It reuses the introduction they own and adds the third person in its cheapest form, `is`.

miniStory.why: Three-way introductions are better felt as a roleplay with a named partner than as a narrated scene.

arcs.autonomyTarget: mid-level: the suggestion is withheld on the integrated episode
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided introductions of a third person, one of them inside a greeting sequence
arcs.risk: Family vocabulary and cultural assumptions. The budget is three neutral relations plus a fallback that needs none, and no episode assumes a family structure.

arcs.communicativeProblem: In a real place the learner cannot ask where anything is, and cannot understand the short answer if somebody tells them.
arcs.whyNow: It is independent of the life-and-people branch, and it converts Pre-A1's naming of things into acting in a place.

miniStory.why: Being lost is a situation with a beginning and an end, and a branch — asking a passer-by or asking at a desk — that is genuinely two valid choices.

arcs.autonomyTarget: mid-level; repair is planted deliberately because the answers carry unknown words
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided location questions, two unaided short answers, one repair used in context
arcs.risk: Directions creep. The arc stops at where-and-near; sequences of turns are A2.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can ask for something politely but cannot find out what it costs, choose between two, or understand a number above ten.
arcs.whyNow: It reuses the counter shape Pre-A1 finished on and adds the money that was missing, with the number extension in the only place it is needed.

miniStory.why: A purchase is the level's clearest whole transaction, and a hosted story can carry the shopkeeper's turns while the learner keeps the decisions.

arcs.autonomyTarget: mid-to-late; the integrated purchase runs with the suggestion withheld
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided price questions, one unaided number above ten, one whole purchase held unaided
arcs.risk: The heaviest arc: a number system, a question form and a transaction. Four episodes, and the numbers arrive as prices rather than as counting.

arcs.titleConcept: What you can and can't do
arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner cannot say what they are able to do, so they cannot accept, decline or explain themselves when something is offered.
arcs.whyNow: Late enough that the question forms are familiar, and it prepares the arrangement arc: an invitation needs an answer about ability.

miniStory.why: Two episodes, and the value is in the learner's own answers rather than in a narrated situation.

arcs.autonomyTarget: late: model answers withheld by default, hints on request
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided ability statements including a negative, and one unaided ability question
arcs.risk: `Can you…?` already exists as a request in Pre-A1. The evaluator must judge the ability sense without breaking the repair sense — the level's one real architectural debt.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can agree that something sounds good but cannot fix when, where, or confirm it — so nothing they arrange actually happens.
arcs.whyNow: Last, because it needs time, place, ability and politeness at once and introduces almost nothing of its own.

miniStory.why: The level's closing situation: a whole arrangement from invitation to confirmation, with a branch where accepting and postponing are both correct.

arcs.autonomyTarget: late: unaided by default; support only after a wrong answer
arcs.evidenceTarget: one whole arrangement held unaided, plus two unaided productions naming a day and a time
arcs.risk: It could become a review episode with a new label. It earns its place only if the learner leaves able to fix a meeting nobody scripted for them.

episodes.productionTarget: the ability question and the how-do-you-say question
episodes.receptiveTarget: an answer that offers a reason, heard only

reuseMatrix.mitigation: The three thin rows are all in the transactions branch. `ask_the_price` and `buy_something` return in the closing arc only as receptive input, so the review scheduler carries them; `ask_about_getting_somewhere` is a should-have and is the first candidate to drop if the level needs trimming.
